transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-04-02 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alice Morgan (Redwood AE), Ben Chu (Redwood SE), Emily Rivera (Praxis Procurement), Tom Anders (CISO), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect), Jordan Lee (Legal)

[00:00] Alice (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alice from Redwood, with Ben our solutions engineer. Quick check, is this still a good time?
[00:05] Emily (Praxis): Yep, good here. Thanks. We have a hard stop around 5:00 PM PT for a leadership check-in but should be ok.
[00:15] Alice: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the approval lifecycle you run for third-party AI vendors, call out the MSA/DPA items you usually flag, and align on what we should prepare for procurement and infosec.
[00:25] Tom (CISO): Sounds good. We'll try to be concise. Our main constraints: data residency for PHI-adjacent metadata, KMS integration, and clear deletion/retention rights.
[00:33] Ben (Redwood SE): Understood. At a high level Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For PHI-adjacent workloads most customers either go dedicated with customer-managed KMS or private VPC deploys. We can talk through tradeoffs.
[00:45] Priya (Cloud): Quick question: what does the private deployment surface look like? VPC peering, transit, or open egress? We try to avoid open egress if possible.
[00:53] Ben: For private we do a customer-managed control plane option; network connectivity can be via private link or peering depending on the cloud. There's a small set of egress endpoints for model pulls, but most inference traffic is inside the VPC. I'm trying to keep the verbatim, but sometimes the transcript garbles a bit, e.g., the note says "K V cash" instead of KV cache.
[01:10] Tom: (laughs) we saw that in an earlier export. Important for us is KMS: we want HSM-backed keys or at least bring-your-own-KMS with key rotation and audit logs.
[01:20] Alice: Yep. Our KMS integrations support cloud KMS and customer-provided keys; HSM can be discussed with our engineering and compliance teams.
[01:30] Jordan (Legal): On the MSA/DPA side, our legal team will primarily look for control over sub-processors and a clear path for deletion on termination. We also have to confirm that Redwood won't use customer inputs for model training unless explicitly permitted.
[01:42] Alice: Totally. Our standard DPA forbids using customer prompts for model training by default, we have an opt-in on that. We can annotate that clearly in the redlines.
[01:50] Emily: Procurement will also need pricing tiers documented. We have a preferred path: start with hosted POC, then move to dedicated, then private if compliance requires. Pricing needs to show delta and forecast impact on monthly spend.
[02:05] Ben: Good. For the POC we usually offer a time-boxed dedicated pool pilot — that's what gives you realistic p95/p99 numbers. We can size it to your token throughput estimates.
[02:15] Priya: About SLA — what are your options? We need something we can map into our vendor scorecard. p99 latency SLO, uptime, and escalation timelines.
[02:25] Ben: We offer three tiers: Hosted (best time-to-value, no SLA), Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity with SLA for availability and p99 latency target), and Private (enterprise-grade SLA + audit). I will share the formal SLA doc, and we can propose a canary/fallback policy in case of regional outages.
[02:40] Tom: On the SLA, do you have objective metrics for p99 at 2k tokens? We need sample numbers to feed into our risk model.
[02:50] Ben: We can produce benchmarks. For example, on a 16k context model a dedicated A100-like pool typically shows p50 30ms, p95 120ms, p99 around 220ms — but that depends on batching. For safety we'll run a benchmark with your prompt distribution.
[03:10] Emily: That would be perfect. Also we need to understand the approval path: who signs MSA, who does security review, and time estimates. In the past our procurement takes 3-4 weeks for vendor review if legal redlines are minor, longer if there's data residency.
[03:25] Alice: So proposed sequence: we send MSA+DPA redlines and SLA tiers by Tue (that's 4/6), Priya and Tom review KMS/arch docs by Mon (4/5), Ben runs the benchmark and shares results next Friday (4/9). Jordan and Redwood legal can do a 30-min call to go over DPA specifics. Does that sequence map to your timelines?
[03:44] Jordan: Yes, that gives us a week to review redlines before the legal committee meeting. One flag: we require explicit sub-processor list or a mechanism to notify for changes.
[03:54] Alice: We can provide current sub-processor list and a 30-day notification commitment, or if necessary an approval workflow for critical sub-processors.
[04:05] Priya: Network — also we need to capture egress costs and whether tokens or payloads leave region. Data residency is a gating item for us; some payloads must remain in eu-central-1.
[04:15] Ben: We support region pinning for dedicated/private. For hosted there are region restrictions; if you need eu-only we recommend dedicated or private. For egress costs, usually those are accounted in dedicated pricing; we'll include estimated data transfer fees in the pricing spreadsheet.
[04:30] Emily: On pricing approvals: we have a two-tier approval: procurement review and a finance sign-off for > $X/month. Can you include expected spend bands depending on load?
[04:40] Alice: Absolutely. We'll include three bands: low, medium, high with projected monthly cost, expected tokens, and recommendation on deployment mode.
[04:50] Tom: A couple of security questions: do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC? And is there an audit trail for API activity with token-level logging?
[04:58] Ben: Yes, we have SSO via SAML and OIDC, role-based access controls with adjustable scopes, and per-token logging in the console with retention configurable. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM. Occasionally the transcript lumps SAML as "SAM L" but it's the same.
[05:15] Emily: Ok. Also procurement will need to know if there are any mandatory insurance clauses or SOC 2 reports we can access.
[05:24] Alice: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and cyber liability insurance details in the data room. I'll attach those docs.
[05:32] Jordan: On the DPA deletion clause, we need an SLA for data removal after termination — 30 days is typical. Any constraints with caches (KV caches, etc)?
[05:44] Ben: We have KV cache eviction controls and on termination we purge caches and can provide attestation. The transcript sometimes says "K V cash" but it's cache. We'll note the technical steps in the redline appendix.
[05:55] Priya: For the POC, will you need sample production prompts? If so, we need to redact PHI. What's the recommended approach?
[06:03] Ben: Best practice is to use synthetic or redacted prompt sets that mirror distribution. We can also run tests inside your environment via private deployment to avoid sending raw data.
[06:15] Tom: We also need a fallback policy in case the dedicated pool is saturated — can you failover to a smaller model or different region?
[06:24] Ben: Yes, we support routing policies: fallback to cheaper or proximate model variants automatically. We'll document the failover latency and quality tradeoffs.
[06:35] Emily: Great. Procurement pathwise, if we get the redlines by 4/6, the legal committee meets on 4/13 so we can aim for decision the week of 4/13 if nothing material changes.
[06:45] Alice: That aligns. Any final blockers?
[06:50] Jordan: One minor: indemnity language. We'll likely propose a cap tied to fees but want to see Redwood's standard.
[06:58] Alice: Noted, we'll include indemnity language and insurance limits in the MSA package.
[07:05] Priya: Also, operational runbooks — how you handle incidents and who is the primary escalation contact? Procurement wants a named on-call or SRE contact for enterprise deals.
[07:16] Ben: For Dedicated and Private we provide a named technical account manager and an escalation chain; we'll include that in the appendix.
[07:25] Emily: Okay, that's helpful. Let's recap the next steps.
[07:30] Alice: Recap: Alice will send MSA/DPA redlines + SLA tiers + pricing bands + SOC2/insurance docs by 2027-04-06. Priya will share network diagrams and SSO/SAML/IAM config by 2027-04-05. Ben will run POC benchmark and share p50/p95/p99 by 2027-04-09. Jordan and Alice to schedule a 30-min DPA deep-dive the week of 4/5. Tom to confirm infosec review owner by 2027-04-07.
[07:52] Tom: All good from our side. We'll try to keep redlines minimal.
[07:58] Emily: Thanks everyone. We'll watch for the deck and documents.
[08:03] Alice: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and booking links for the legal sync.
[08:10] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional misattributions and phonetic errors (e.g., K V cash, SAM L), filler words preserved. Speakers sometimes overlap.

Referenced artifacts/links (to be attached in follow-up):
- MSA+DPA redline draft (to be sent)
- SLA tiers spreadsheet (to be sent)
- SOC 2 Type II report (link)
- Sample benchmark plan and runbook (Ben to produce)

End of transcript.
